items.title: "Am I a candidate for magic mushrooms?" A mystery shopper study of Oregon psilocybin service centers.

summaries.en: Oregon just became the first US state to let people access supervised psilocybin services legally—and researchers wanted to know: what's actually happening? They called 22 licensed centers pretending to be people seeking help for depression. The good news? Every single center took safety seriously, asking detailed questions about psychiatric history and never pushing anyone to stop antidepressants. But here's the catch: the median cost is $1,900 per session, and many centers are struggling financially under licensing fees. This mystery shopper study reveals a system that's playing it cautious—which protects people—but might be pricing out those who need it most. As psychedelics move from underground to regulated spaces, Oregon's early experiment shows us both the promise and the real-world challenges ahead.
summaries.da: Oregon blev lige det første amerikanske stat, der tillader lovlig, overvåget psykedelika-behandling—og forskere ville vide: hvad sker der egentlig? De ringede til 22 licenserede centre og udgav sig for at være mennesker, der søgte hjælp for depression. Den gode nyhed? Hvert eneste center tog sikkerhed seriøst, stillede detaljerede spørgsmål om psykiatrisk historie og pressede aldrig nogen til at stoppe antidepressiva. Men der er en hage: mediankostnaden er $1.900 pr. session, og mange centre kæmper økonomisk med licensgebyrer. Dette mystery shopper-studie viser os et system, der spiller det sikkert—som beskytter mennesker—men muligvis udelukker dem, der har størst brug for det. Mens psykedelika bevæger sig fra underjorden til regulerede rum, viser Oregons tidlige eksperiment både løftet og de virkelige udfordringer forude.

items.title: AI-assisted characterization of psychedelic clinical trials from ClinicalTrials.gov

summaries.en: There are now over 400 clinical trials testing psychedelics for mental health — and psilocybin is leading the charge, with depression as the top target. Researchers used AI to map this explosive growth across ClinicalTrials.gov, finding psilocybin in 244 trials, MDMA in 99, and LSD, DMT, and other compounds filling out the landscape. A team connected an AI language model directly to the trial registry to pull and organize this messy, sprawling data automatically — something that would take humans months to do by hand. This snapshot reveals where psychedelic medicine is actually heading: depression and PTSD are the clinical frontlines, and the field is moving fast enough that AI is now the only practical way to keep track. Welcome to the new era of psychedelic research.
summaries.da: Der findes nu over 400 kliniske forsøg, der tester psykedelika mod psykiske lidelser — og psilocybin fører an, med depression som det vigtigste mål. Forskere brugte kunstig intelligens til at kortlægge denne eksplosive vækst på ClinicalTrials.gov og fandt psilocybin i 244 forsøg, MDMA i 99, og LSD, DMT og andre stoffer udfylder landskabet. Et team forbandt en AI-sprogmodel direkte til forsøgsregistret for automatisk at trække og organisere denne rodet, spredt data — noget der ville tage mennesker måneder at gøre manuelt. Dette øjebliksbillede afslører, hvor psykedelisk medicin faktisk er på vej: depression og PTSD er de kliniske frontlinjer, og området udvikler sig så hurtigt, at AI nu er den eneste praktiske måde at følge med på. Velkommen til psykedelisk forskeringens nye æra.

items.title: [Connectome and Depression: Towards Precision Psychiatry Based on Brain Networks].

summaries.en: Scientists are mapping the brain's wiring to finally understand why depression hits different people in different ways—and more importantly, which treatments will actually work for *you*. A new review shows that brain scan patterns can reveal whether someone will respond to therapy, antidepressants, or even ketamine, opening a door to truly personalized mental healthcare instead of trial-and-error guessing. Researchers analyzed brain imaging studies looking at how depression disrupts key networks involved in mood, reward, and decision-making. The takeaway? We're moving toward "precision psychiatry"—medicine tailored to your brain, not a one-size-fits-all approach. It's still early, and real clinical challenges remain, but understanding these neural patterns is a fundamental shift that could transform how we treat depression.
summaries.da: Forskere kortlægger hjernens forbindelser for endelig at forstå, hvorfor depression rammer forskellige mennesker på forskellige måder—og vigtigere: hvilken behandling der faktisk virker for *dig*. En ny oversigt viser, at hjernescans kan afsløre, om man reagerer på terapi, antidepressiva eller endda ketamin, og åbner døren til virkelig personaliseret psykisk sundhedssorg i stedet for prøve-og-fejl. Forskere analyserede hjernebillede-studier, der kiggede på, hvordan depression forstyrrer vigtige netværk involveret i stemning, belønning og beslutningstagning. Konklusionen? Vi bevæger os mod "præcisions-psykiatri"—medicin skræddersyet til din hjerne, ikke en løsning der passer alle. Det er stadig tidligt, og rigtige kliniske udfordringer består, men forståelsen af disse neurale mønstre er et fundamentalt skift, der kan transformere, hvordan vi behandler depression.

items.title: Salud intercultural en Pastaza: regulación del uso de plantas medicinales y de la ayahuasca

summaries.en: Ayahuasca has been used for centuries in Amazonian communities, but when taken outside that cultural context—like in retreat centers around the world—the risks multiply fast. A new study examining legal frameworks and scientific evidence in Ecuador's Pastaza region found a troubling gap: while indigenous medicine is constitutionally recognized, there are zero specific safety standards, dosing guidelines, or protections for traditional knowledge. The research reviewed international law, ethnobotanical data, and clinical evidence to understand how psychedelics like ayahuasca should actually be regulated. The conclusion? We need rules created *with* indigenous communities and knowledge keepers, not imposed from outside. This matters because it points toward a smarter future where psychedelics are respected both as powerful medicines and as part of living cultures.
summaries.da: Ayahuasca er blevet brugt i århundreder i amazonske samfund, men når det tages uden for den kulturelle sammenhæng—som på retreats rundt omkring i verden—stiger risiciene hurtigt. Et nyt studie af juridiske rammer og videnskabelig evidens i Ecuadors Pastaza-region afslørede et bekymrende hul: selvom oprindelig medicin er forfatningsmæssigt anerkendt, findes der nul specifikke sikkerhedsstandarder, doseringsretningslinjer eller beskyttelse af traditionel viden. Forskningen gennemgik international lov, etnobotaniske data og klinisk evidens for at forstå, hvordan psykedelika som ayahuasca egentlig bør reguleres. Konklusionen? Vi har brug for regler skabt *sammen med* oprindelige samfund og videnskeepere, ikke påtvunget udefra. Dette betyder noget, fordi det peger mod en smartere fremtid, hvor psykedelika respekteres både som kraftfulde mediciner og som del af levende kulturer.

items.title: Feeling safe: an empirical-ethical analysis of vulnerability in (es)ketamine treatment.

summaries.en: When you take ketamine in a clinical setting, your mind opens up—but so does your vulnerability. A new study reveals something crucial: patients undergoing ketamine treatment need more than just medical safety; they need to *feel* safe. Researchers interviewed 14 patients and 10 clinicians across German psychiatric clinics to understand what actually makes people feel protected during these powerful experiences. The findings show that trust in your surroundings, understanding what's happening to you, and genuine connection with your care team aren't luxuries—they're essential ingredients for treatment to work. This research fits perfectly into where psychedelic science is heading: moving beyond "does it work?" to "how do we create the best possible conditions for healing?" As ketamine and other consciousness-altering treatments gain clinical traction, getting the human side of care right is just as important as the medicine itself.
summaries.da: Når du tager ketamin i en klinisk setting, åbner dit sind sig—men det gør din sårbarhed også. Et nyt studie afslører noget afgørende: patienter i ketaminbehandling har brug for mere end bare medicinsk sikkerhed; de har brug for at *føle sig* sikre. Forskere interviewede 14 patienter og 10 klinikere på tværs af tyske psykiatriske klinikker for at forstå, hvad der faktisk gør mennesker beskyttet under disse kraftfulde oplevelser. Fundet viser, at tillid til dine omgivelser, forståelse for hvad der sker med dig, og ægte kontakt med dit behandlungsteam ikke er luksus—det er væsentlige ingredienser for, at behandlingen virker. Denne forskning passer perfekt ind i hvor psykedelika-forskningen er på vej hen: fra "virker det?" til "hvordan skaber vi de bedst mulige betingelser for helbredelse?" Når ketamin og andre bevidsthedsomdannende behandlinger vinder klinisk indpas, er det menneskelige aspekt af pleje lige så vigtig som medicinen selv.

items.title: Antidepressants and Cognitive Function in Major Depressive Disorder: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Implications for Precision Treatment.

summaries.en: Depression doesn't just make you sad—it fogs your thinking. A new review reveals that while traditional antidepressants can help clear that fog, they work differently for different people. Some drugs like vortioxetine show real promise for sharpening focus and memory, while others help specific thinking skills. The catch? We're still not sure if they're fixing your brain directly or just helping you think better once the depression lifts. Researchers looked at decades of studies to map out how antidepressants affect cognition through multiple pathways—from boosting brain chemicals to reducing inflammation. Here's what's exciting: the review hints at emerging treatments like ketamine and psychedelics as potential game-changers for the thinking problems that often stick around even after mood improves. This points toward a future where we match the right treatment to each person's specific needs.
summaries.da: Depression påvirker ikke bare dit humør—det tåger også dit tænkning. Et nyt overblik viser, at selvom traditionelle antidepressiva kan hjælpe med at rydde denne tåge, virker de forskelligt for forskellige mennesker. Nogle lægemidler som vortioxetin viser rigtig potentiale for at skærpe fokus og hukommelse, mens andre hjælper bestemte kognitive evner. Øjet? Vi er stadig usikre på, om de reparerer din hjerne direkte eller bare hjælper dig til at tænke bedre, når depressionen Letter. Forskere gennemgik årtiers studier for at kortlægge, hvordan antidepressiva påvirker kognitionen gennem flere veje—fra styrkelse af hjernekemikalier til reduktion af inflammation. Her er det spændende: oversigten antyder, at kommende behandlinger som ketamin og psykedelika kunne være game-changere for tænkningsproblemer, der ofte hænger ved, selv efter humøret bliver bedre. Dette peger mod en fremtid, hvor vi matcher den rigtige behandling til hver persons specifikke behov.

items.title: Investigating molecular and hemodynamic effects of LSD in the human brain.

summaries.en: For the first time, scientists have directly observed how LSD actually works inside the human brain using cutting-edge brain imaging. The findings? LSD latches onto specific receptors and dramatically increases blood flow throughout the brain, while simultaneously making different brain regions talk less to each other. What's fascinating is that your subjective experience—the trip itself—doesn't simply follow the drug levels in your bloodstream, suggesting LSD's magic involves more complex mechanisms than previously understood. Researchers used PET-MRI scanners on volunteers to map these effects, then compared LSD's fingerprint to psilocybin (magic mushrooms), revealing both striking similarities and important differences. This kind of precise molecular mapping is exactly what psychedelic medicine needs right now: concrete data showing *how* these compounds actually engage with our brains, which helps scientists design better treatments and understand why psychedelics show such promise for conditions like depression and PTSD.
summaries.da: For første gang har forskere direkte observeret, hvordan LSD virker inde i menneskets hjerne ved hjælp af avanceret hjerneafbildning. Resultaterne? LSD binder sig til specifikke receptorer og øger blodgennemstrømningen dramatisk overalt i hjernen, mens det samtidig får forskellige hjernedele til at kommunikere mindre med hinanden. Det fascinerende er, at din subjektive oplevelse—turen selv—følger ikke blot det stof, der cirkulerer i dit blod, hvilket tyder på, at LSD's virkning involverer mere komplekse mekanismer end tidligere antaget. Forskere brugte PET-MRI-scannere på frivillige til at kortlægge disse effekter og sammenlignede derefter LSD's fingeraftryk med psilocybin (tryllesvampe), hvilket afslørede både slående ligheder og vigtige forskelle. Netop denne præcise molekylære kortlægning er præcis det, psykedelisk medicin har brug for nu: konkrete data, der viser *hvordan* disse stoffer faktisk kommunikerer med vores hjerner, hvilket hjælper forskere med at udvikle bedre behandlinger og forstå, hvorfor psykedelika viser så stor løfte for tilstande som depression og PTSD.

items.title: Enhancing cGMP signaling with psilocybin reduces head twitch and restructures the synaptic proteome while maintaining antidepressant response.

summaries.en:
What if we could get the antidepressant benefits of psilocybin without the intense perceptual effects that make some people hesitant? New research suggests it might be possible. Scientists found that combining psilocybin with a compound that boosts a specific brain signaling pathway (cGMP) reduced the characteristic "head twitch" response in rodents—a marker of psilocybin's perceptual effects—while keeping the antidepressant benefits intact.

The team used a targeted approach to dampen one pathway while letting another flourish, essentially fine-tuning how psilocybin works in the brain. This sits at the heart of where psychedelic research is heading: moving beyond "does it work?" to "can we make it work better and safer for more people?" If these findings translate to humans, we're looking at a potential future where psychedelic therapy becomes more accessible and tolerable—a significant step forward in treating depression.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis vi kunne få psykedelikas antidepressive effekt uden de intense oplevelsesmæssige virkninger, der gør nogle mennesker usikre? Ny forskning tyder på, at det kunne være muligt. Forskere opdagede, at kombination af psilocybin med et stof, der øger en specifik hjernesignalvej (cGMP), reducerede det karakteristiske "head twitch"-svar hos gnavere—en markør for psilocybins oplevelsesmæssige effekter—mens antidepressive fordele blev bevaret.

Teamet brugte en målrettet tilgang til at dæmpe én vej, mens de lod en anden blomstrer op, og gjorde således præcis justering af, hvordan psilocybin virker i hjernen. Dette ligger i hjertet af, hvor psykedelika-forskning er på vej hen: videre fra "virker det?" til "kan vi få det til at virke bedre og sikrere for flere mennesker?" Hvis disse fund kan overføres til mennesker, ser vi en potentiel fremtid, hvor psykedelisk terapi bliver mere tilgængelig og tolerabel—et væsentligt skridt fremad i behandlingen af depression.

items.title: Augmentation strategies for intravenous ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

summaries.en:
Ketamine is a game-changer for people with treatment-resistant depression—it works fast when everything else has failed. But here's the catch: the relief doesn't always last. A new analysis of seven studies tested whether adding other treatments to ketamine could make the effects stick around longer or work even better. The results? Most add-ons didn't deliver what researchers hoped for, though talk therapy and a specific training technique showed some early promise for keeping the benefits going.

This systematic review looked at seven randomized controlled trials involving 346 people, comparing ketamine plus various augmentation strategies against ketamine plus placebo. What's exciting is that this research highlights exactly where psychedelic science is heading: beyond just finding drugs that work, we're learning how to make those breakthroughs last. The field is shifting from "Does it work?" to "How do we maximize it?"—and that's when treatments truly transform lives.
summaries.da:
Ketamin er et vendepunkt for mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression—det virker hurtigt når alt andet har fejlet. Men her er hagen: lettelsen holder ikke altid. En ny analyse af syv studier testede, om det at tilføje andre behandlinger til ketamin kunne få effekterne til at vare længere eller virke endnu bedre. Resultatet? De fleste tilføjelser leverede ikke, hvad forskere håbede på, selvom samtalebehandling og en specifik træningsmetode viste nogle tidlige tegn på at bevare fordelene.

Denne systematiske oversigt kiggede på syv randomiserede kontrolforsøg med 346 mennesker og sammenlignede ketamin plus forskellige tilføjelsesstrategier med ketamin plus placebo. Det spændende er, at denne forskning viser præcis, hvor psykedelika-forskningen går hen: ud over bare at finde stoffer, der virker, lærer vi hvordan man maksimerer dem. Feltet skifter fra "Virker det?" til "Hvordan får vi mest ud af det?"—og det er når behandlinger virkelig forandrer liv.

items.title: Психоделічно-асистована терапія: ретроспективний огляд і сучасні перспективи

summaries.en:
We're witnessing a remarkable shift: psychedelics that were sidelined for decades are now proving genuinely effective in clinical settings for depression, anxiety, PTSD, and addiction—with some patients experiencing breakthroughs where conventional treatments failed. What changed? Better brain science, smarter research methods, and a willingness to revisit what indigenous cultures have known for centuries.

A new review traces this journey from ancient healing practices through the mid-20th century experiments to today's psychedelic renaissance, showing how careful studies on psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, and ayahuasca are reshaping mental healthcare. The research reveals something crucial: the drug itself is only part of the story—your mindset and the therapeutic setting matter enormously. As leading research centers worldwide expand their programs, we're entering an era where psychedelics aren't counterculture mythology anymore, but a serious frontier in treating conditions that affect millions.
summaries.da:
Vi er vidne til en bemærkelsesværdig vending: psykedelika, som blev fejet til side i årtier, viser sig nu genuint effektive i kliniske settings mod depression, angst, PTSD og afhængighed—nogle patienter oplever gennembrud, hvor almindelig behandling slog fejl. Hvad ændrede sig? Bedre hjerneforskning, smartere forskningsmetoder og vilje til at genoverveje, hvad oprindelige kulturer har vidst siden længe.

En ny gennemgang følger denne rejse fra gamle helbredelsespraktikker gennem forsøg i midten af det 20. århundrede til dagens psykedeliske renæssance, og viser hvordan nøje studier på psilocybin, MDMA, LSD og ayahuasca omformer psykiatrisk behandling. Forskningen afslører noget afgørende: selve stoffet er kun halvdelen af historien—din mentale indstilling og den terapeutiske ramme betyder enormt meget. Mens førende forskningscentre verden over ekspanderer deres programmer, træder vi ind i en æra, hvor psykedelika ikke længere er modkultur-mytologi, men en seriøs frontier for at behandle tilstande, som påvirker millioner.

items.title: Ketamine administered biomedically or as psychedelic-assisted therapy in treatment-resistant depression: Differing efficacy based on depressive subtype or presence of childhood trauma?

summaries.en: What if depression isn't one thing? New research suggests ketamine might work differently depending on your type of depression—and whether you experienced childhood trauma. Researchers found that medical ketamine alone showed more promise for melancholic depression, while ketamine paired with therapy could be the better fit for other presentations. This matters because we've long treated depression as a single diagnosis with a single solution, but emerging evidence says that's not how our brains work. The study opens a crucial door: as psychedelics move from curiosity to medicine, personalizing treatment based on individual differences could transform outcomes. This is where real precision psychiatry begins.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis depression ikke er én ting? Ny forskning tyder på, at ketamin kan virke forskelligt afhængigt af din depressionstype—og om du oplevede traumer i barndommen. Forskerne fandt, at medicinsk ketamin alene viste større effekt ved melankoli depression, mens ketamin kombineret med terapi kunne være bedre for andre udforminger. Det betyder noget, fordi vi længe har behandlet depression som én diagnose med én løsning, men stigende bevis siger, at det ikke er sådan vores hjerner fungerer. Studiet åbner en afgørende dør: når psykedelika udvikler sig fra nysgerrighed til medicin, kan personalisering af behandling baseret på individuelle forskelle transformere resultaterne. Her begynder rigtig præcisionsbpsykiatri.

items.title: A living systematic review, meta-analysis, and open data resource of trials of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD.

summaries.en: New research shows that MDMA-assisted therapy cuts PTSD symptoms more than twice as effectively as placebo—and helps people actually recover, not just feel a bit better. In fact, people receiving MDMA therapy were 2.25 times more likely to fully remit from PTSD. Scientists analyzed six rigorous clinical trials with 286 participants to reach these findings. This living review is crucial because psychedelic research moves fast, and tracking what actually works matters as MDMA-assisted therapy edges closer to becoming a regulated treatment. We're seeing concrete evidence that this approach deserves serious attention in psychiatry—not hype, just solid science showing real hope for people stuck with trauma.
summaries.da: Ny forskning viser, at MDMA-assisteret terapi reducerer PTSD-symptomer mere end dobbelt så effektivt som placebo—og hjælper mennesker til faktisk at blive raske, ikke bare føle sig lidt bedre. Folk i behandling med MDMA var faktisk 2,25 gange mere tilbøjelige til fuldstændigt at blive symptomfri for PTSD. Forskere analyserede seks stringente kliniske forsøg med 286 deltagere for at nå disse resultater. Dette løbende review er afgørende fordi psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig hurtigt, og det betyder noget at følge med i, hvad der faktisk virker, når MDMA-assisteret terapi nærmer sig godkendelse som ordinær behandling. Vi ser konkrete beviser for, at denne tilgang fortjener alvorlig opmærksomhed inden for psykiatri—ikke hype, bare solid videnskab der giver ægte håb til mennesker, der sidder fast med traumer.

items.title: Drug arrests and seizures in Japan, 2015-2025 (National Police Agency)

summaries.en: Japan's drug enforcement data just got a major spotlight—not because arrests are skyrocketing, but because it reveals something crucial about how different countries handle psychedelics as medicine becomes real. As psilocybin enters Phase 3 clinical trials globally, Japan's regulatory approach stands in sharp contrast to countries rethinking drug policy. This dataset, tracking arrests and seizures from 2015-2025, shows the messy reality: while some nations debate therapeutic access, enforcement remains the default in others. The data tells a human story about timing—people seeking treatment options today might live in a country where the science is approved tomorrow, or never. Researchers compiled this to expose regulatory fragmentation: the same molecule, studied in clinical trials, remains criminalized in different ways across borders. It's a wake-up call that access to future psychedelic medicines won't depend solely on science, but on which country you call home. Understanding these gaps is the first step toward fairer, more evidence-based drug policy.
summaries.da: Japans narkotikahåndhævelsesdata får nu massiv opmærksomhed—ikke fordi arrestationerne eksploderer, men fordi det afslører noget afgørende om, hvordan forskellige lande håndterer psykedelika når medicinen bliver virkelighed. Mens psilocybin går ind i fase 3-forsøg globalt, står Japans regulatoriske tilgang i skarp kontrast til lande, der genovervejer narkotikapolitik. Dette datasæt, som følger arrestationer og beslaglæggelser fra 2015-2025, viser den rodede virkelighed: mens nogle nationer debatterer terapeutisk adgang, er håndhævelse stadig standarden andre steder. Data fortæller en menneskelig historie om timing—mennesker, der søger behandlingsmuligheder i dag, kan leve i et land hvor videnskaben godkendes i morgen, eller aldrig. Forskere samlede dette for at blotlægge regulatorisk fragmentering: samme molekyle, studeret i kliniske forsøg, forbliver kriminaliseret på forskellige måder på tværs af grænserne. Det er en vækkekald om, at adgang til fremtidige psykedelika-medicin ikke kun afhænger af videnskab, men af hvilket land du kalder hjem. At forstå disse huller er første skridt mod mere retfærdig og evidensbaseret narkotikapolitik.

items.title: Psychedelics and Sleep: Preclinical and Human Studies—A Systematic Review

summaries.en: What happens to your sleep when you take psychedelics? New research shows something fascinating: classic psychedelics like LSD and psilocybin mess with your REM sleep in the short term—delaying it, reducing it, and keeping you more awake through the night. But here's the twist: when people actually report back on how they slept, many say it didn't feel that bad, and some even notice their sleep problems improve in the weeks after. Scientists reviewed 12 studies combining lab work and real-world observations to piece together this puzzle. This matters because sleep is where your brain processes emotions and builds new connections—exactly what psychedelics are supposed to help with. As psychedelics move closer to becoming real treatments for depression and anxiety, understanding these sleep changes is becoming crucial to getting the timing and dosing just right.
summaries.da: Hvad sker der med din søvn når du tager psykedelika? Ny forskning viser noget fascinerende: klassiske psykedelika som LSD og psilocybin rocker op i din REM-søvn på kort sigt—de forsinker det, reducerer det og holder dig mere vågen gennem natten. Men her er vendingen: når mennesker faktisk rapporterer tilbage om hvordan de sov, siger mange at det ikke var så slemt, og nogle bemærker endda at deres søvnproblemer bliver bedre i ugerne efter. Forskere gennemgik 12 studier kombineret laboratoriearbejde og virkelighedsobservationer for at løse gåden. Det betyder noget fordi søvn er hvor din hjerne behandler følelser og bygger nye forbindelser—præcis hvad psykedelika skal hjælpe med. Når psykedelika nærmer sig at blive rigtige behandlinger for depression og angst, bliver det afgørende at forstå disse søvnændringer for at få timing og dosering præcis rigtig.

items.title: Adverse reactions to psychedelics in naturalistic settings are associated with current psychopathology and well-being: A correlational study.

summaries.en:
New research reveals something important: people who experience difficult reactions to psychedelics often share something in common — they're already struggling with anxiety, depression, or other mental health challenges. The study tracked over 1,000 people who used psychedelics outside clinical settings and found that bad trips weren't random; they clustered among those dealing with current psychological strain. Younger users and those taking psychedelics frequently also reported more trouble.

Scientists collected this data through detailed online surveys, mapping how adverse reactions connect to mental health, setting, and who you're with when you trip. This matters because as psychedelics move toward medical use, we're learning that preparation and screening matter enormously — it's not just about the substance itself, but about meeting people where they are psychologically. This research adds crucial real-world evidence to what therapists have long suspected: set and setting aren't luxuries, they're foundational to safety.
summaries.da:
Ny forskning afslørede noget vigtigt: mennesker, der oplever vanskelige reaktioner på psykedelika, har ofte noget til fælles — de kæmper allerede med angst, depression eller andre psykiske udfordringer. Studiet fulgte over 1.000 personer, som brugte psykedelika uden for kliniske rammer, og fandt ud af, at dårlige ture ikke var tilfældige; de koncentrerede sig blandt dem, der håndterede nuværende psykisk belastning. Yngre brugere og dem, som tog psykedelika ofte, rapporterede også mere besvær.

Forskere indsamlede denne data gennem detaljerede onlineundersøgelser, der kortlagde, hvordan uønskede reaktioner forbinder sig til mental sundhed, setting og hvem du er sammen med, når du tager psykedelika. Det betyder noget, fordi mens psykedelika bevæger sig mod medicinsk brug, lærer vi, at forberedelse og screening betyder enormt meget — det handler ikke kun om stoffet selv, men om at møde mennesker dér, hvor de er psykologisk. Denne forskning tilføjer vigtig virkelighed til det, som terapeuter længe har mistankt: set og setting er ikke luksus, de er grundlæggende for sikkerhed.

items.title: Subcutaneous Esketamine in Adolescents with Severe Depressive Episodes: A Five-Case Series.

summaries.en:
What happens when a teenager struggling with severe depression and suicidal thoughts tries esketamine—a fast-acting relative of the anesthetic ketamine? A new study followed five young people (ages 15-17) who received eight weekly injections after other treatments had failed. The results were mixed but encouraging: one achieved full remission, three improved significantly, and even the one who didn't improve still saw their suicidal thoughts decrease. The treatment was well-tolerated, with only minor side effects like brief dissociative moments or slight blood pressure changes—nothing severe.

Researchers used a straightforward observational approach, simply tracking how these adolescents responded over the eight-week course. This small study adds to a growing body of evidence that psychedelics and their cousins might offer real hope for young people in psychiatric crisis when nothing else works. We're still in the early stages, but glimpses like this suggest esketamine deserves serious attention as part of our toolkit for severe adolescent depression.
summaries.da:
Hvad sker der, når en teenager, der kæmper med alvorlig depression og selvmordstanker, prøver esketamin—en hurtigvirkende kusine til anæstetikummet ketamin? Et nyt studie fulgte fem unge mennesker (15-17 år), der fik otte ugentlige injektioner, efter at andre behandlinger havde slået fejl. Resultaterne var blandede, men opløftende: én opnåede fuldstændig remission, tre blev betydeligt bedre, og selv den ene, der ikke blev bedre, oplevede et fald i selvmordstanker. Behandlingen blev godt tolereret med kun mindre bivirkninger som kortvarige dissociative øjeblikke eller let blodtryksstigning—intet alvorligt.

Forskerne brugte en ligetil observationsmetode og sporede simpelthen, hvordan disse adolescenter responderede over otte uger. Dette lille studie bidrager til voksende beviser for, at psykedelika og deres slægtninge kan være rigtig håb for unge mennesker i psykiatrisk krise, når intet andet virker. Vi er stadig i de tidlige stadier, men glimt som dette tyder på, at esketamin fortjener alvorlig opmærksomhed som del af vores værktøj mod alvorlig depression hos unge.

items.title: Intercultural pathways to indigenous mental health: the integration of ayahuasca in community care in the Yaqui intercultural medicine clinic in Sonora, Mexico

summaries.en: Indigenous communities in Mexico are getting mental healthcare on their own terms. A new clinic in Sonora integrated ayahuasca into a healing program led by Yaqui healers and therapists together, combining ceremony, counseling, sweat lodges, and cultural practices like language and music. Early results show it works—and matters, because Indigenous people face huge mental health gaps that traditional Western medicine alone hasn't solved. Researchers documented how the clinic was built and what happened when 130 patients received care this way, using both traditional measurements and their own community standards to track healing. This model is important because psychedelic research has mostly ignored Indigenous knowledge systems and who should actually be leading this work. As science catches up to what Indigenous communities have always known, studies like this show the real path forward: psychedelics aren't just a Western medicine story—they're part of a much older conversation about what healing can be.
summaries.da: Oprindelige samfund i Mexico får nu mental sundhedsvejledning på deres egne præmisser. En ny klinik i Sonora integrerede ayahuasca i et helbredsprogram ledet af yaqui-healers og terapeuter sammen, der kombinerede ceremonier, rådgivning, svedehytter og kulturelle praksisser som sprog og musik. Tidlige resultater viser, at det virker—og det betyder noget, fordi oprindelige mennesker står over for massiv mental sundhedskrise, som vestlig medicin alene ikke har løst. Forskere dokumenterede, hvordan klinikken blev bygget og hvad der skete, da 130 patienter fik behandling på denne måde, ved at bruge både traditionelle målinger og deres eget samfunds standarder til at måle helbredelse. Denne model er vigtig, fordi psykedelika-forskning stort set har ignoreret oprindelige kundesystemer og hvem der faktisk skulle lede dette arbejde. Når videnskaben indhenter det, som oprindelige samfund altid har vidst, viser studier som dette den rigtige vej fremad: psykedelika er ikke kun en vestlig medicin-historie—de er del af en meget ældre samtale om, hvad helbredelse kan være.

items.title: Policy Watch: FDA moves toward clinical trials of the psychedelic ibogaine

summaries.en:
The FDA is taking ibogaine seriously. This West African plant medicine, traditionally used in spiritual ceremonies, is moving into formal clinical trials—a huge shift in how Western medicine views psychedelics. Ibogaine shows remarkable potential for treating addiction, especially opioid dependence, where conventional treatments often fall short. What does this mean for you? It could eventually offer people struggling with addiction a genuinely different path forward, one grounded in rigorous science rather than stigma.

This policy shift reflects where psychedelic research is heading right now: from underground experiments to mainstream medicine. The FDA's move signals growing recognition that these substances deserve serious investigation, not dismissal. As more psychedelics enter the clinical pipeline, we're building the evidence base that could reshape how we treat mental health and addiction. Ibogaine's journey from taboo to trial is a turning point worth watching.
summaries.da:
FDA tager ibogain alvorligt. Dette vestafrikanske plantemiddel, traditionelt brugt i spirituelle ceremonier, bevæger sig nu ind i formelle kliniske forsøg—en kæmpe skift i, hvordan vestlig medicin ser på psykedelika. Ibogain viser bemærkelsesværdig potentiale til at behandle afhængighed, især opioidafhængighed, hvor konventionelle behandlinger ofte svigter. Hvad betyder det for dig? Det kunne på sigt give mennesker, der kæmper med afhængighed, en virkelig anderledes vej frem, grundfestet i seriøs videnskab i stedet for stigma.

Dette politiske skifte afspejler, hvor psykedelika-forskning er på vej hen: fra underjordiske eksperimenter til mainstream medicin. FDA's handling signalerer stigende anerkendelse af, at disse stoffer fortjener seriøs undersøgelse, ikke afvisning. Når flere psykedelika kommer ind i den kliniske pipeline, bygger vi det vidensgrundlag, der kunne omforme, hvordan vi behandler mental sundhed og afhængighed. Ibogains rejse fra tabu til forsøg er et vendepunkt værd at følge.

items.title: Psychedelics in neurosurgery: Potential utility in prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation

summaries.en: Imagine facing brain surgery while battling depression, anxiety, and chronic pain on top of everything else. New research suggests psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD could transform how we care for neurosurgery patients—reducing psychological suffering, managing pain, and even helping people recover lost abilities. Scientists reviewed evidence from 2020-2026 across psychedelics including psilocybin, LSD, ketamine, and others, finding psilocybin produces lasting relief from cancer-related depression and anxiety, while other compounds show promise for trauma recovery and pain. No one's given these to neurosurgery patients yet, but the evidence from related fields is compelling enough that researchers are now asking: shouldn't we explore this possibility? This could represent a major shift in how we support people through one of life's most challenging medical experiences.
summaries.da: Forestil dig at skulle gennem hjerneoperation mens du kæmper med depression, angst og kroniske smerter. Ny forskning tyder på, at psykedelika som psilocybin og LSD kunne revolutionere, hvordan vi passer på neurokirurgiske patienter—ved at reducere psykisk lidelse, håndtere smerte og hjælpe folk med at få evner tilbage. Forskere gennemgik evidens fra 2020-2026 på tværs af psykedelika som psilocybin, LSD, ketamin og andre og fandt, at psilocybin giver varig lindring fra kræftrelateret depression og angst, mens andre stoffer viser løfte for traumagendannelse og smertehåndtering. Ingen har endnu givet disse midler til neurokirurgiske patienter, men beviserne fra relaterede felter er overbevisende nok til, at forskere nu stiller spørgsmålet: burde vi ikke udforske denne mulighed? Dette kunne repræsentere et stort skift i, hvordan vi støtter mennesker gennem en af livets mest udfordrende medicinske erfaringer.

items.title: Direct Quantitation of Psilocybin and Psilocin by 1H and 31P qNMR in Wild Psilocybe from Greece

summaries.en:
Scientists just measured psilocybin levels in wild Greek mushrooms using a new, rapid technique — and they found something significant: this is the first officially documented psychoactive Psilocybe species recorded in Greece in peer-reviewed science. The study developed a faster way to analyze psilocybin and psilocin using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), a method that could become crucial for quality control and research as clinical trials with psychedelics accelerate worldwide.

This matters because right now, psilocybin is tightly controlled in most places, which makes it hard to get standardized reference materials for labs and courts. By developing better detection methods and cataloguing wild species, researchers are laying groundwork that could help speed up clinical development, ensure safety, and support the growing body of evidence that psychedelics have real therapeutic potential for brain health.
summaries.da:
Forskere har netop målt psykedelika-niveauer i vilde græske svampe ved hjælp af en ny, hurtig teknik — og de fandt noget betydeligt: det er første gang en psykoaktiv Psilocybe-art officielt er dokumenteret fra Grækenland i peer-reviewed videnskab. Studiet udviklede en hurtigere metode til at analysere psilocybin og psilocin ved hjælp af kernmagnetisk resonans (NMR), en teknik som kunne blive afgørende for kvalitetskontrol og forskning, når kliniske forsøg med psykedelika accelererer verden over.

Dette betyder noget, fordi psilocybin i dag er stærkt kontrolleret de fleste steder, hvilket gør det svært at få standardiserede referencematerialer til laboratorierne og domstolene. Ved at udvikle bedre detektionsmetoder og katalogisere ville arter lægger forskerne grundlaget for at kunne fremskynde klinisk udvikling, sikre sikkerhed og understøtte det voksende bevis for, at psykedelika har reel terapeutisk potentiale for hjernens sundhed.
